audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim mourning, food distinction, and tithe law, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for mourning-body practices, clean/unclean land and water animals, birds, carrion, kid-in-milk prohibition, annual tithe pilgrimage, monetary conversion, Levite inclusion, and third-year tithe for vulnerable residents.

verses.restored: Children are you to YHWH your Divine. You shall not cut yourselves or make baldness between your eyes for the dead.

familiar.text: Ye are the children of the LORD your God: ye shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead.

modern.text: You are sons of the LORD your God; do not cut yourselves or shave your foreheads on behalf of the dead,

original.text: בָּנִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם לֹ֣א תִתְגֹּֽדְד֗וּ וְלֹֽא תָשִׂ֧ימוּ קָרְחָ֛ה בֵּ֥ין עֵינֵיכֶ֖ם לָמֵֽת

verses.restored: For a holy people are you to YHWH your Divine, and YHWH chose you to be for him a treasured people from all peoples upon face of ground.

familiar.text: For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God, and the LORD hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.

modern.text: for you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD has chosen you to be a people for His prized possession out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.

original.text: כִּ֣י עַ֤ם קָדוֹשׁ֙ אַתָּ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וּבְךָ֞ בָּחַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לִֽהְי֥וֹת לוֹ֙ לְעַ֣ם סְגֻלָּ֔ה מִכֹּל֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה

verses.restored: You shall not eat any abominable thing.

familiar.text: Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing.

modern.text: You must not eat any detestable thing.

original.text: לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל כָּל תּוֹעֵבָֽה

verses.restored: These are animals you may eat: ox, sheep, and goat,

familiar.text: These are the beasts which ye shall eat: the ox, the sheep, and the goat,

modern.text: These are the animals that you may eat: The ox, the sheep, the goat,

original.text: זֹ֥את הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאכֵ֑לוּ שׁ֕וֹר שֵׂ֥ה כְשָׂבִ֖ים וְשֵׂ֥ה עִזִּֽים

verses.restored: deer, gazelle, roebuck, wild goat, ibex, antelope, and mountain sheep.

familiar.text: The hart, and the roebuck, and the fallow deer, and the wild goat, and the pygarg, and the wild ox, and the chamois.

modern.text: the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.

original.text: אַיָּ֥ל וּצְבִ֖י וְיַחְמ֑וּר וְאַקּ֥וֹ וְדִישֹׁ֖ן וּתְא֥וֹ וָזָֽמֶר

verses.restored: Every animal dividing hoof, cleaving two clefts, and chewing cud among animals, it you may eat.

familiar.text: And every beast that parteth the hoof, and cleaveth the cleft into two claws, and cheweth the cud among the beasts, that ye shall eat.

modern.text: You may eat any animal that has a split hoof divided in two and that chews the cud.

original.text: וְכָל בְּהֵמָ֞ה מַפְרֶ֣סֶת פַּרְסָ֗ה וְשֹׁסַ֤עַת שֶׁ֨סַע֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י פְרָס֔וֹת מַעֲלַ֥ת גֵּרָ֖ה בַּבְּהֵמָ֑ה אֹתָ֖הּ תֹּאכֵֽלוּ

verses.restored: Yet these you shall not eat among those chewing cud or dividing cleft hoof: camel, hare, and rock badger, for they chew cud but do not divide hoof; unclean they are for you.

familiar.text: Nevertheless these ye shall not eat of them that chew the cud, or of them that divide the cloven hoof; as the camel, and the hare, and the coney: for they chew the cud, but divide not the hoof; therefore they are unclean unto you.

modern.text: But of those that chew the cud or have a completely divided hoof, you are not to eat the following: the camel, the rabbit, or the rock badger. Although they chew the cud, they do not have a divided hoof. They are unclean for you,

original.text: אַ֣ךְ אֶת זֶ֞ה לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמַּֽעֲלֵ֣י הַגֵּרָ֔ה וּמִמַּפְרִיסֵ֥י הַפַּרְסָ֖ה הַשְּׁסוּעָ֑ה אֶֽת הַ֠גָּמָל וְאֶת הָאַרְנֶ֨בֶת וְאֶת הַשָּׁפָ֜ן כִּֽי מַעֲלֵ֧ה גֵרָ֣ה הֵ֗מָּה וּפַרְסָה֙ לֹ֣א הִפְרִ֔יסוּ טְמֵאִ֥ים הֵ֖ם לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: And pig, for it divides hoof but does not chew cud; unclean it is for you. From their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcass you shall not touch.

familiar.text: And the swine, because it divideth the hoof, yet cheweth not the cud, it is unclean unto you: ye shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their dead carcase.

modern.text: as well as the pig; though it has a divided hoof, it does not chew the cud. It is unclean for you. You must not eat its meat or touch its carcass.

original.text: וְאֶת הַ֠חֲזִיר כִּֽי מַפְרִ֨יס פַּרְסָ֥ה הוּא֙ וְלֹ֣א גֵרָ֔ה טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶ֑ם מִבְּשָׂרָם֙ לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֔לוּ וּבְנִבְלָתָ֖ם לֹ֥א תִגָּֽעוּ

verses.restored: These you may eat from all in waters: everything having fins and scales you may eat.

familiar.text: These ye shall eat of all that are in the waters: all that have fins and scales shall ye eat:

modern.text: Of all the creatures that live in the water, you may eat anything with fins and scales,

original.text: אֶת זֶה֙ תֹּֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמָּ֑יִם כֹּ֧ל אֲשֶׁר ל֛וֹ סְנַפִּ֥יר וְקַשְׂקֶ֖שֶׂת תֹּאכֵֽלוּ

verses.restored: Whatever has no fins and scales you shall not eat; unclean it is for you.

familiar.text: And whatsoever hath not fins and scales ye may not eat; it is unclean unto you.

modern.text: but you may not eat anything that does not have fins and scales; it is unclean for you.

original.text: וְכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֵֽין ל֛וֹ סְנַפִּ֥יר וְקַשְׂקֶ֖שֶׂת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: You shall not eat anything that dies of itself. To sojourner within your gates you may give it and he may eat it, or you may sell it to foreigner, for a holy people are you to YHWH your Divine. You shall not boil a kid in milk of its mother.

familiar.text: Ye shall not eat of anything that dieth of itself: thou shalt give it unto the stranger that is in thy gates, that he may eat it; or thou mayest sell it unto an alien: for thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother’s milk.

modern.text: You are not to eat any carcass; you may give it to the foreigner residing within your gates, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner. For you are a holy people belonging to the LORD your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk. Giving Tithes (Leviticus 27:30–34; Deuteronomy 26:1–15; Nehemiah 13:10–14)

original.text: לֹ֣א תֹאכְל֣וּ כָל נְ֠בֵלָה לַגֵּ֨ר אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֜יךָ תִּתְּנֶ֣נָּה וַאֲכָלָ֗הּ א֤וֹ מָכֹר֙ לְנָכְרִ֔י כִּ֣י עַ֤ם קָדוֹשׁ֙ אַתָּ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽא תְבַשֵּׁ֥ל גְּדִ֖י בַּחֲלֵ֥ב אִמּֽוֹ

familiar.text: Thou shalt truly tithe all the increase of thy seed, that the field bringeth forth year by year.

modern.text: You must be sure to set aside a tenth of all the produce brought forth each year from your fields.

original.text: עַשֵּׂ֣ר תְּעַשֵּׂ֔ר אֵ֖ת כָּל תְּבוּאַ֣ת זַרְעֶ֑ךָ הַיֹּצֵ֥א הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה שָׁנָ֥ה שָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: You shall eat before YHWH your Divine, in place he chooses to cause his name to dwell, tithe of grain, new wine, oil, and firstborn of herd and flock, so you may learn to fear/revere YHWH your Divine all days.

familiar.text: And thou shalt eat before the LORD thy God, in the place which he shall choose to place his name there, the tithe of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the firstlings of thy herds and of thy flocks; that thou mayest learn to fear the LORD thy God always.

modern.text: And you are to eat a tenth of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the LORD your God at the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.

original.text: וְאָכַלְתָּ֞ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ בַּמָּק֣וֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר֮ לְשַׁכֵּ֣ן שְׁמ֣וֹ שָׁם֒ מַעְשַׂ֤ר דְּגָֽנְךָ֙ תִּֽירֹשְׁךָ֣ וְיִצְהָרֶ֔ךָ וּבְכֹרֹ֥ת בְּקָרְךָ֖ וְצֹאנֶ֑ךָ לְמַ֣עַן תִּלְמַ֗ד לְיִרְאָ֛ה אֶת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ כָּל הַיָּמִֽים

familiar.text: And if the way be too long for thee, so that thou art not able to carry it; or if the place be too far from thee, which the LORD thy God shall choose to set his name there, when the LORD thy God hath blessed thee:

modern.text: But if the distance is too great for you to carry that with which the LORD your God has blessed you, because the place where the LORD your God will choose to put His Name is too far away,

original.text: וְכִֽי יִרְבֶּ֨ה מִמְּךָ֜ הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ כִּ֣י לֹ֣א תוּכַ֘ל שְׂאֵתוֹ֒ כִּֽי יִרְחַ֤ק מִמְּךָ֙ הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִבְחַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לָשׂ֥וּם שְׁמ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם כִּ֥י יְבָרֶכְךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: then you shall turn it into silver, bind silver in your hand, and go to place YHWH your Divine chooses.

familiar.text: Then shalt thou turn it into money, and bind up the money in thine hand, and shalt go unto the place which the LORD thy God shall choose:

modern.text: then exchange it for money, take the money in your hand, and go to the place the LORD your God will choose.

original.text: וְנָתַתָּ֖ה בַּכָּ֑סֶף וְצַרְתָּ֤ הַכֶּ֨סֶף֙ בְּיָ֣דְךָ֔ וְהָֽלַכְתָּ֙ אֶל הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בּֽוֹ

verses.restored: You shall give silver for whatever your soul/life desires—for cattle, flock, wine, strong drink, or anything your soul/life asks—and you shall eat there before YHWH your Divine and rejoice, you and your household.

familiar.text: And thou shalt bestow that money for whatsoever thy soul lusteth after, for oxen, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, or for whatsoever thy soul desireth: and thou shalt eat there before the LORD thy God, and thou shalt rejoice, thou, and thine household,

modern.text: Then you may spend the money on anything you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything you wish. You are to feast there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice with your household.

original.text: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה הַכֶּ֡סֶף בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר תְּאַוֶּ֨ה נַפְשְׁךָ֜ בַּבָּקָ֣ר וּבַצֹּ֗אן וּבַיַּ֨יִן֙ וּבַשֵּׁכָ֔ר וּבְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּֽשְׁאָלְךָ֖ נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְאָכַ֣לְתָּ שָּׁ֗ם לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֖ אַתָּ֥ה וּבֵיתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: The Levite within your gates you shall not abandon, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.

familiar.text: And the Levite that is within thy gates; thou shalt not forsake him; for he hath no part nor inheritance with thee.

modern.text: And do not neglect the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.

original.text: וְהַלֵּוִ֥י אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תַֽעַזְבֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין ל֛וֹ חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: At end of three years you shall bring out all tithe of your produce in that year and place it within your gates.

familiar.text: At the end of three years thou shalt bring forth all the tithe of thine increase the same year, and shalt lay it up within thy gates:

modern.text: At the end of every three years, bring a tenth of all your produce for that year and lay it up within your gates.

original.text: מִקְצֵ֣ה שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֗ים תּוֹצִיא֙ אֶת כָּל מַעְשַׂר֙ תְּבוּאָ֣תְךָ֔ בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִ֑וא וְהִנַּחְתָּ֖ בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Then Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, and sojourner, orphan, and widow within your gates shall come and eat and be satisfied, so YHWH your Divine may bless you in all work of your hand that you do.

familiar.text: And the Levite, (because he hath no part nor inheritance with thee,) and the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, which are within thy gates, shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied; that the LORD thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hand which thou doest.

modern.text: Then the Levite (because he has no portion or inheritance among you), the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow within your gates may come and eat and be satisfied. And the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.

original.text: וּבָ֣א הַלֵּוִ֡י כִּ֣י אֵֽין לוֹ֩ חֵ֨לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֜ה עִמָּ֗ךְ וְ֠הַגֵּר וְהַיָּת֤וֹם וְהָֽאַלְמָנָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ וְאָכְל֖וּ וְשָׂבֵ֑עוּ לְמַ֤עַן יְבָרֶכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶֽׂה

translation_notes: Mourning practices are regulated as identity markers; the law must not shame grief, hair loss, scars, cultural mourning, or people who self-injure and need care.
The food list belongs to Israel's dietary holiness tradition and later Jewish kashrut; it must not be mocked, superseded, or imposed on non-Jews.
Species identifications for several birds are uncertain and require lexical/zoological audit.
The rule concerning carrion distinguishes Israelite holiness practice from sojourner/foreigner food economy; it should not be used to demean immigrants.
The pilgrimage tithe includes practical monetary conversion and household rejoicing.
The third-year tithe turns agricultural wealth into local food security for Levite, immigrant, orphan, and widow.
safety_note: Do not use Deuteronomy 14 to stigmatize grieving bodies, shame eating practices, demean Jewish kashrut, or treat immigrants as inferior. Center holiness as disciplined identity and tithing as shared food, joy, and material provision for vulnerable neighbors.
